```{=html}
<!--
Purpose
- This is a maintainable refactor of the exploratory obesity/HRF analysis.
- It preserves the same conceptual outputs as the 2026-05-07 PDF draft:
  data checks, variable derivations, attrition, descriptive tables, BMI-category plots,
  primary/sensitivity logistic models, hypercapnia subgroup model, and first-pass PAF/PIF.
- It intentionally centralizes constants and helper functions before use.
- It avoids treating missing gas data as "No HRF".
-->
```

# Analysis plan

Primary question: among encounters with recorded BMI and classifiable hypercapnic respiratory failure (HRF) status, estimate the association between BMI and HRF and estimate model-standardized impact fractions under BMI counterfactuals.

Primary outcome: stringent hypercapnic respiratory failure, defined by ventilatory support plus either ABG or VBG evidence of hypercapnic acidosis.

Sensitivity outcome: strict lab + ICD hypercapnic respiratory failure.

Primary PIF/PAF approach: fit an adjusted logistic regression model, then standardize predicted risk under observed BMI and under named counterfactual BMI distributions.

```{r constants}
# Clinical cutoffs. Keep these in one location so any future edits are deliberate.
CO2_ABG_CUTOFF <- 45
CO2_VBG_CUTOFF <- 50
PH_CUTOFF <- 7.35
OBESITY_CUTOFF <- 30
NORMAL_BMI_COUNTERFACTUAL <- 25

ICD_HRF_VARS <- c("has_j9612", "has_j9622", "has_j9692", "has_j9602")

PRIMARY_MODEL_FORMULA <- hrf_v1 ~ curr_bmi_num + age_at_encounter + sex + ethnicity
STRICT_MODEL_FORMULA <- hrf_v2_strict ~ curr_bmi_num + age_at_encounter + sex + ethnicity
HYPERCAPNIA_SUBGROUP_FORMULA <- hrf_vs_comp ~ curr_bmi_num + age_at_encounter + sex + ethnicity

BMI_CATEGORY_LEVELS <- c(
  "Underweight",
  "Normal weight",
  "Overweight",
  "Obesity I",
  "Obesity II",
  "Obesity III"
)

COEF_MAP_COMMON <- c(
  "curr_bmi_num" = "BMI (per 1 kg/m^2)",
  "age_at_encounter" = "Age (per year)",
  "sexMale" = "Male",
  "ethnicityHispanic or Latino" = "Hispanic/Latino",
  "ethnicityUnknown" = "Ethnicity: Unknown"
)

# Preferred location. Keep a fallback for the current exploratory file layout.
DATA_PATH_CANDIDATES <- c(
  here::here("data", "raw", "full_db.rds"),
  here::here("full_db.rds")
)
```

# Helper functions

```{r helpers-validation}
require_columns <- function(data, columns, data_name = "data") {
  missing_columns <- setdiff(columns, names(data))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(
      sprintf(
        "%s is missing required columns: %s",
        data_name,
        paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  invisible(data)
}

first_existing_path <- function(paths) {
  existing <- paths[file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(existing) == 0) {
    stop(
      "Could not find the analysis dataset. Tried:\n  ",
      paste(paths, collapse = "\n  "),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  existing[[1]]
}

as_binary_from_labelled <- function(x, positive_label, negative_label) {
  x_label <- as.character(haven::as_factor(x))
  dplyr::case_when(
    x_label == positive_label ~ 1,
    x_label == negative_label ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
}

parse_numeric_bmi <- function(x) {
  x_chr <- stringr::str_trim(as.character(haven::zap_labels(x)))
  x_chr <- dplyr::na_if(x_chr, "n/a")
  valid_numeric <- stringr::str_detect(x_chr, "^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?$")
  dplyr::if_else(valid_numeric, as.numeric(x_chr), NA_real_)
}

make_bmi_category <- function(bmi) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(bmi) ~ NA_character_,
    bmi < 18.5 ~ "Underweight",
    bmi < 25 ~ "Normal weight",
    bmi < 30 ~ "Overweight",
    bmi < 35 ~ "Obesity I",
    bmi < 40 ~ "Obesity II",
    bmi >= 40 ~ "Obesity III"
  ) |>
    factor(levels = BMI_CATEGORY_LEVELS)
}
```

```{r helpers-derivation}
standardize_raw_data <- function(raw_data) {
  required <- c(
    "curr_bmi",
    "niv_proc",
    "imv_proc",
    "highest_paco2",
    "abg_ph",
    "vbg_co2",
    "vbg_ph",
    "age_at_encounter",
    "sex",
    "ethnicity",
    ICD_HRF_VARS
  )
  require_columns(raw_data, required, "raw_data")

  raw_data |>
    mutate(
      niv_proc = as_binary_from_labelled(
        niv_proc,
        positive_label = "Received NIV (not including nightly CPAP)",
        negative_label = "No NIV"
      ),
      imv_proc = as_binary_from_labelled(
        imv_proc,
        positive_label = "Received IMV",
        negative_label = "No IMV"
      ),
      curr_bmi_num = parse_numeric_bmi(curr_bmi),
      highest_paco2 = as.numeric(highest_paco2),
      abg_ph = as.numeric(abg_ph),
      vbg_co2 = as.numeric(vbg_co2),
      vbg_ph = as.numeric(vbg_ph),
      sex = haven::as_factor(sex) |> forcats::fct_na_value_to_level(level = "Unknown or Other"),
      ethnicity = haven::as_factor(ethnicity) |> forcats::fct_na_value_to_level(level = "Unknown")
    )
}

derive_analysis_variables <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(
      # Availability flags. These are used by attrition, outcome classification, and missingness checks.
      has_bmi = !is.na(curr_bmi_num),
      has_abg_pair = !is.na(highest_paco2) & !is.na(abg_ph),
      has_vbg_pair = !is.na(vbg_co2) & !is.na(vbg_ph),
      has_any_gas_pair = has_abg_pair | has_vbg_pair,
      received_ventilation = niv_proc == 1 | imv_proc == 1,

      bmi_category = make_bmi_category(curr_bmi_num),
      obesity_bmi30 = curr_bmi_num >= OBESITY_CUTOFF,

      abg_hypercapnia = has_abg_pair & highest_paco2 >= CO2_ABG_CUTOFF,
      vbg_hypercapnia = has_vbg_pair & vbg_co2 >= CO2_VBG_CUTOFF,
      physiologic_hypercapnia = abg_hypercapnia | vbg_hypercapnia,

      abg_hypercapnic_acidosis = abg_hypercapnia & abg_ph <= PH_CUTOFF,
      vbg_hypercapnic_acidosis = vbg_hypercapnia & vbg_ph <= PH_CUTOFF,
      lab_hypercapnic_acidosis = abg_hypercapnic_acidosis | vbg_hypercapnic_acidosis,

      hrf_v1_numeric = case_when(
        received_ventilation & lab_hypercapnic_acidosis ~ 1,
        has_any_gas_pair ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      hrf_v1 = factor(hrf_v1_numeric, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),

      compensated_hypercapnia = case_when(
        abg_hypercapnia & abg_ph > PH_CUTOFF ~ 1,
        vbg_hypercapnia & vbg_ph > PH_CUTOFF ~ 1,
        has_any_gas_pair ~ 0,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),

      # Mutually exclusive clinical status. This avoids leaving compensated hypercapnia hidden inside "No HRF".
      respiratory_status = case_when(
        hrf_v1_numeric == 1 ~ "HRF",
        compensated_hypercapnia == 1 ~ "Compensated hypercapnia",
        has_any_gas_pair & !physiologic_hypercapnia ~ "No hypercapnia",
        has_any_gas_pair ~ "Other classifiable gas pattern",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ) |>
        factor(levels = c("No hypercapnia", "Compensated hypercapnia", "HRF", "Other classifiable gas pattern")),

      hrf_labs_v2 = as.integer(lab_hypercapnic_acidosis),
      hrf_icd_v2 = as.integer(rowSums(across(all_of(ICD_HRF_VARS), ~ as.numeric(.x) == 1), na.rm = TRUE) > 0),
      hrf_v2 = as.integer(hrf_labs_v2 == 1 | hrf_icd_v2 == 1),
      hrf_v2_strict = as.integer(hrf_labs_v2 == 1 & hrf_icd_v2 == 1),

      # Broad definition for descriptive question: hypercapnia by ABG/VBG CO2 or ICD flag.
      hypercapnia_any = as.integer(physiologic_hypercapnia | hrf_icd_v2 == 1)
    )
}
```

```{r helpers-tables-models}
make_missingness_table <- function(data, variables) {
  require_columns(data, variables, "data")

  tibble(variable = variables) |>
    mutate(
      n_missing = map_int(variable, ~ sum(is.na(data[[.x]]))),
      n_present = map_int(variable, ~ sum(!is.na(data[[.x]]))),
      n_total = n_missing + n_present,
      pct_missing = round(100 * n_missing / n_total, 1)
    )
}

make_attrition_table <- function(data, primary_cohort, strict_cohort, hypercapnia_cohort) {
  tibble(
    step = c(
      "Source dataset",
      "BMI recorded",
      "BMI recorded + classifiable gas pair",
      "Primary analytic cohort (BMI + classifiable HRF v1)",
      "Strict v2 sensitivity cohort",
      "Physiologic hypercapnia subgroup"
    ),
    n = c(
      nrow(data),
      sum(data$has_bmi, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(data$has_bmi & data$has_any_gas_pair, na.rm = TRUE),
      nrow(primary_cohort),
      nrow(strict_cohort),
      nrow(hypercapnia_cohort)
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      n_excluded_from_previous_step = c(NA_real_, -diff(n)),
      pct_of_source = round(100 * n / first(n), 1)
    )
}

make_bmi_outcome_summary <- function(data, outcome, event_value = "Yes") {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na(bmi_category), !is.na(.data[[outcome]])) |>
    group_by(bmi_category) |>
    summarise(
      n_total = n(),
      n_event = sum(.data[[outcome]] == event_value, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_non_event = n_total - n_event,
      pct_event = round(100 * n_event / n_total, 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(bmi_category)
}

fit_logistic_model <- function(formula, data) {
  stats::glm(formula, data = data, family = stats::binomial())
}

estimate_pif <- function(model, label, bmi_counterfactual) {
  # Use the model frame to ensure predictions use exactly the complete-case analytic rows used by glm().
  model_data <- stats::model.frame(model)

  observed_risk <- mean(stats::predict(model, newdata = model_data, type = "response"), na.rm = TRUE)

  counterfactual_data <- model_data
  counterfactual_data$curr_bmi_num <- bmi_counterfactual(counterfactual_data$curr_bmi_num)
  counterfactual_risk <- mean(stats::predict(model, newdata = counterfactual_data, type = "response"), na.rm = TRUE)

  tibble(
    counterfactual = label,
    n_model_rows = nrow(model_data),
    risk_observed = observed_risk,
    risk_counterfactual = counterfactual_risk,
    pif = (observed_risk - counterfactual_risk) / observed_risk
  )
}

make_standardized_bmi_curve <- function(model, bmi_values) {
  model_data <- stats::model.frame(model)

  map_dfr(bmi_values, function(bmi_value) {
    prediction_data <- model_data
    prediction_data$curr_bmi_num <- bmi_value

    tibble(
      curr_bmi_num = bmi_value,
      predicted_risk = mean(stats::predict(model, newdata = prediction_data, type = "response"), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  })
}
```

```{r helpers-plots}
theme_paper <- function(base_size = 10) {
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

plot_bmi_category_summary <- function(summary_data, title, y_label) {
  ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = bmi_category, y = pct_event)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75, fill = "grey65") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct_event, "%")), vjust = -0.35, size = 3) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "BMI category",
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_paper() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
}

plot_standardized_bmi_curve <- function(curve_data) {
  ggplot(curve_data, aes(x = curr_bmi_num, y = predicted_risk)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(25, 30, 40), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(
      title = "Adjusted predicted probability of HRF across BMI",
      x = "BMI (kg/m^2)",
      y = "Model-standardized predicted risk"
    ) +
    theme_paper()
}

plot_pif_results <- function(pif_results) {
  pif_results |>
    mutate(counterfactual = forcats::fct_reorder(counterfactual, pif)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = pif, y = counterfactual)) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    labs(
      title = "Model-standardized impact fraction estimates",
      x = "Impact fraction",
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_paper() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}
```

# Cohorts and attrition

```{r define-cohorts}
primary_cohort <- analysis_data |>
  filter(has_bmi, !is.na(hrf_v1))

strict_cohort <- analysis_data |>
  filter(
    has_bmi,
    has_any_gas_pair,
    hrf_v2_strict == 1 | (hrf_labs_v2 == 0 & hrf_icd_v2 == 0)
  )

hypercapnia_cohort <- analysis_data |>
  filter(
    has_bmi,
    has_any_gas_pair,
    physiologic_hypercapnia
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hrf_vs_comp = case_when(
      hrf_v1 == "Yes" ~ 1,
      compensated_hypercapnia == 1 ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(hrf_vs_comp))
```

attrition_table <- make_attrition_table(

)

# Primary and sensitivity models

```{r fit-primary-models}
model_primary_unadjusted <- fit_logistic_model(hrf_v1 ~ curr_bmi_num, primary_cohort)
model_primary_adjusted <- fit_logistic_model(PRIMARY_MODEL_FORMULA, primary_cohort)

model_strict_unadjusted <- fit_logistic_model(hrf_v2_strict ~ curr_bmi_num, strict_cohort)
model_strict_adjusted <- fit_logistic_model(STRICT_MODEL_FORMULA, strict_cohort)

model_hypercapnia_subgroup <- fit_logistic_model(HYPERCAPNIA_SUBGROUP_FORMULA, hypercapnia_cohort)
```

```{r primary-model-tables}
modelsummary(
  list(
    "HRF v1: unadjusted" = model_primary_unadjusted,
    "HRF v1: adjusted" = model_primary_adjusted,
    "HRF v2 strict: unadjusted" = model_strict_unadjusted,
    "HRF v2 strict: adjusted" = model_strict_adjusted
  ),
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  statistic = "conf.int",
  ci_method = "wald",
  coef_map = COEF_MAP_COMMON,
  gof_omit = "RMSE|F|Adj|R2"
)
```

```{r hypercapnia-subgroup-model}
modelsummary(
  list("HRF vs compensated hypercapnia" = model_hypercapnia_subgroup),
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  statistic = "conf.int",
  ci_method = "wald",
  coef_map = COEF_MAP_COMMON,
  gof_omit = "RMSE|F|Adj|R2"
)
```

# Population attributable fraction / impact fraction

This section uses model standardization. The current exploratory PDF used the counterfactual "set everyone to BMI 25". That is retained as a proof-of-concept row, but the more interpretable obesity estimands cap BMI above a threshold while leaving lower BMI values unchanged.

```{r pif-estimates}
pif_primary <- bind_rows(
  estimate_pif(
    model_primary_adjusted,
    label = "Proof of concept: set everyone to BMI 25",
    bmi_counterfactual = function(bmi) rep(NORMAL_BMI_COUNTERFACTUAL, length(bmi))
  ),
  estimate_pif(
    model_primary_adjusted,
    label = "Excess BMI: BMI >25 set to 25",
    bmi_counterfactual = function(bmi) pmin(bmi, 25)
  ),
  estimate_pif(
    model_primary_adjusted,
    label = "Obesity: BMI >30 set to 30",
    bmi_counterfactual = function(bmi) pmin(bmi, 30)
  ),
  estimate_pif(
    model_primary_adjusted,
    label = "Severe obesity: BMI >40 set to 40",
    bmi_counterfactual = function(bmi) pmin(bmi, 40)
  )
) |>
  mutate(target_population = "Primary analytic cohort", .before = counterfactual)

pif_primary
```

```{r severe-obesity-subgroup-pif}
severe_obesity_cohort <- primary_cohort |>
  filter(curr_bmi_num >= 40)

model_severe_obesity <- fit_logistic_model(PRIMARY_MODEL_FORMULA, severe_obesity_cohort)

pif_severe_obesity_subgroup <- estimate_pif(
  model_severe_obesity,
  label = "BMI >=40 subgroup: BMI >40 set to 40",
  bmi_counterfactual = function(bmi) pmin(bmi, 40)
) |>
  mutate(target_population = "BMI >=40 subgroup", .before = counterfactual)

# Under a linear PIF-vs-excess-BMI approximation, this gives the average PIF contribution per BMI point above 40.
mean_bmi_excess_above_40 <- mean(stats::model.frame(model_severe_obesity)$curr_bmi_num - 40, na.rm = TRUE)

pif_severe_obesity_subgroup |>
  mutate(
    mean_bmi_excess_above_40 = mean_bmi_excess_above_40,
    approximate_pif_per_bmi_point_above_40 = pif / mean_bmi_excess_above_40
  )
```

```{r pif-results-table}
pif_results <- bind_rows(pif_primary, pif_severe_obesity_subgroup)

pif_results |>
  mutate(
    across(c(risk_observed, risk_counterfactual, pif), ~ round(.x, 4))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Target population",
      "Counterfactual",
      "Model rows",
      "Observed risk",
      "Counterfactual risk",
      "Impact fraction"
    ),
    caption = "Model-standardized impact fractions under named BMI counterfactuals."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-pif
#| fig-cap: "Model-standardized impact fraction estimates under BMI counterfactuals."
#| fig-alt: "Dot plot showing impact fraction estimates for several BMI counterfactual definitions."
plot_pif_results(pif_primary)
```

# Adjusted BMI-risk curve

```{r bmi-risk-curve-data}
bmi_grid <- seq(
  from = floor(quantile(primary_cohort$curr_bmi_num, probs = 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)),
  to = ceiling(quantile(primary_cohort$curr_bmi_num, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = 1
)

bmi_risk_curve <- make_standardized_bmi_curve(model_primary_adjusted, bmi_grid)
bmi_risk_curve
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-bmi-risk-curve
#| fig-cap: "Adjusted predicted HRF risk across BMI using standardization over the primary model covariate distribution."
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of standardized predicted HRF risk by BMI with reference lines at BMI 25, 30, and 40."
plot_standardized_bmi_curve(bmi_risk_curve)
```
